text:
paul_sales: DeltaCorp POC -- customer reports very slow first-token and occasional 429s during burst tests. They've got a week left on the evaluation. Can eng swarm?
cam_eng: on it. can you paste the request pattern? avg prompt length, concurrency during burst?
paul_sales: most requests are short single-turn prompts (~30–60 tokens). burst test hits ~120 concurrent requests for 30s. We saw first-token ~700ms -> sometimes >1.5s. 429s at peak.
cam_eng: initial hypothesis: batching wait + cold KV cache. Short prompts + high concurrency often create two problems: runtime waits to fill big batches (increasing first-token) and cache misses cause extra decode overhead.
jamal_sre: also check client-side concurrency spikes. If they backoff too slowly, our token-bucket can hit burst limits -> 429s. logs?
paul_sales: attaching brief snippet from their load run (copied):
```
[2026-01-17T14:03:21Z] request_id=rpc-0a3a session=delta-123 seq=1 prompt_tokens=45 total_tokens=45 latency_first=820ms status=200
[2026-01-17T14:03:22Z] request_id=rpc-0a3b session=delta-124 seq=1 prompt_tokens=38 total_tokens=38 latency_first=1580ms status=200
[2026-01-17T14:03:23Z] request_id=rpc-0a3c session=delta-125 seq=1 prompt_tokens=52 total_tokens=52 latency_first=320ms status=429
```
cam_eng: ok, that matches batching wait skew. Two immediate ops: reduce max_wait_ms or enable adaptive batching, and prewarm/kvcache the most common prefixes. Example config we can suggest on the Dedicated/Hosted runtime: 
```yaml
serving:
  batching:
    mode: adaptive
    target_batch_size: 16
    max_wait_ms: 10    # lower the wait to avoid large batch fill latencies for short prompts
  concurrency:
    max_in_flight: 200
  cache:
    prefix_cache: enabled
    ttl_minutes: 60
```
nina_ml: for prefix cache, we can push a warmup job that issues the top 1000 canonical prompts once before their spike window. simple script: 
```
# warmup script (pseudo)
for p in top_prompts.txt:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/respond -d '{"input": "'"$p"'"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <$KEY>"
```
jamal_sre: for the 429s: either increase token-bucket for their API key (temporary surge credit) or put them on a small Dedicated pool for the POC. Dedicated avoids shared rate limits. Which does sales want?
anne_sales: customer asked about cost impact if we do prewarm + larger concurrency. need a quick pricing delta to confirm.
cam_eng: quick back-of-envelope: warmup 1k requests -> ~50k tokens. At hosted rates that's tiny (~$X). Dedicated pool estimate depends on reserved slots; for a 2-hour burst window we could use burst credits (metered) — rough extra $Y for the week. I'll get exact numbers from finance but it's low compared to deal.
paul_sales: can we do temporary burst credit + adaptive batching now so they can finish POC tomorrow?
cam_eng: yes. Ops checklist: 1) set batching.mode=adaptive + max_wait_ms=10 2) enable prefix_cache, ttl 60m 3) grant delta POC +20% token-bucket for 24h 4) run warmup script 30m before the next run. I can apply 1–3, but need security sign-off for step 4 if customer data is sensitive (we're sending prompts).
sec-qa-bot: Sec checklist for any warmup using customer prompts: must confirm PII policy and KMS key usage; warmup requests should route via the customer's VPC/Private deployment if data is sensitive.
paul_sales: customer has a redacted prompt set (no PII) they can provide. They also dropped a security questionnaire that needs answers on encryption-at-rest, KMS, SOC2 date.
nina_ml: for spectroscopy: enabling prefix_cache doesn't store raw prompts in plaintext in our hot cache — it stores hashed keys + KV. we should document that for the questionnaire.
jamal_sre: I'll pull current SOC2 report and KMS integration summary. give me 2 hours.
paul_sales: perfect. last: any runtime tweak that risks model quality? do we change sampling/temperature? customer worried prewarm might bias outputs.
cam_eng: warmup just populates KV/past keys for speed; it doesn't change model weights or sampling. adaptive batching reduces wait but preserves ordering. no quality change expected. we can run A/B for 500 requests to verify.
anne_sales: I'll tell them we can apply adaptive batching + temporary burst credits now, run warmup with their redacted prompts, and answer security QA within the day. they want confirmation in 2 hours.
deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: "batching-adaptive" config -> 5% -> monitor first_token_latency, errors.
cam_eng: starting canary now, watching 1-min traces. I'll update when stable.
paul_sales: thanks all. will ping customer and share ETA. :thumbsup:
cam_eng: canary stable after 3m, first-token median dropped from 760ms -> 210ms in initial sampling, 429s gone for those runs.
paul_sales: incredible — customer notified, preparing follow-up demo tonight.
jamal_sre: uploaded SOC2 snapshot + KMS notes to the shared drive: https://redwood.internal/secure/soc2-delta-poc (restricted).
paul_sales: closing loop. if anything flares up ping here.
anne_sales: nice win, team. :tada:
